title: District heating peak reduction under varying supply temperatures

publication.title: A Modular Co-Simulation Platform for Comparing Flexibility Solutions in District Heating Under Variable Operating Conditions

sources.title: Mazzarino et al. (2025), district heating flexibility co-simulation

limitations: No executable code, FMU file, or simulation input dataset (time series / network files) supplied in the artifact — prevents runtime verification.
Thermal storage FMU export/validation details (tests comparing original Modelica model vs FMU) are not provided.
Control strategies are described as 'semi-optimized' or rule-based; no optimization algorithm or full pseudo-code is present.
Results derive from a single case study topology and specific DSM/storage schedules; generalizability to other networks is not demonstrated.
Time‑shifted exchange is described as an approximation; numerical/temporal error bounds or initialization procedure details are not provided.

findings.claim: Framework purpose: modular Plug&Play MOSAIK co-simulation platform to compare TES and DSM flexibility strategies in district heating under varying supply temperatures.
findings.explanation: Paper explicitly states the framework purpose in Abstract and Introduction.

findings.claim: Co-simulation engine: MOSAIK orchestrator and MOSAIK Python APIs manage synchronization, instantiation and data-exchange.
findings.explanation: Section II-B and Fig. 1 describe MOSAIK use and roles.

findings.claim: Operational Layer includes: Thermal power plant (Python), DH grid (1-D quasi-steady Python model; Eqs. 1–3), Thermal storage (AixLib Modelica-derived FMU exposing Charging/Discharging temp & mass-flow, External temp, Top/Bottom temps), Control strategy (Python), Weather and Building as time-series readers.
findings.explanation: Paper lists models, implementation types and TES FMU I/O in Section II-B and Fig. 3; DH equations are provided as (1)–(3).

findings.claim: Directional exchanges and sequence: preliminary Control→(Storage schedule or Building anticipatory profile) and numbered calculation flows as in Fig. 4 (Building → plant+grid; Weather→storage; Storage→plant+grid when charging/discharging; Plant→grid; Grid→Building+Storage; Building→Grid return; Grid→Plant).
findings.explanation: Fig. 4 and Section II‑C explicitly enumerate and describe the numbered message flows.

findings.claim: Most simulators use 60 s time step; Thermal storage FMU stepped every 10 s; framework uses time‑shifted messaging to resolve cyclic data flows.
findings.explanation: Section IV-B and Fig. 8 show execution graph and state that storage is stepped at 10 s while others at 60 s; time-shifted exchange is discussed.

findings.claim: Case study: radial delivery sub-network (202 nodes / 201 edges), 47 buildings, 1 thermal storage (~26,150 L), 1 thermal power plant; simulations run for supply temperatures 120, 110, 100, 90 °C.
findings.explanation: Section III and figures/tables describe the topology, counts, storage capacity, and supply temperature scenarios.

findings.claim: Control strategies implemented: (i) TES schedule — charge 03:00–05:20 at ~3.094 kg/s and discharge ~06:00–07:00 with variable flow proportional to peak slope; (ii) DSM — advance selected building load profiles (majority by 30 minutes; Table I shows per-building advance distribution).
findings.explanation: Paper gives charge/discharge schedule and DSM shift configuration; authors state schedules are not mathematically optimized.

findings.claim: Reported peak reduction: Storage strategy declines with lower inlet temperature (example values: 18.04% at 120 °C → 14.95% at 90 °C). DSM produces roughly constant reduction (~33–34%) across supply temperatures; maximum DSM variation ~1.22 percentage points.
findings.explanation: Section IV discusses and Table II (with Fig. 6) provides the numeric/visual results and the quoted percentages.

findings.claim: Modified AixLib Modelica tank exported to FMU — equivalence to original Modelica model and numerical validation are assumed but not shown.
findings.locator: §II-B, p. 411 (statement: 'modifications only regard the interfaces ... without affecting the validity of the underlying physical model from AixLib')
findings.explanation: Authors state interface-only modifications but provide no validation data comparing FMU vs original Modelica model.
findings.recommended_correction: Record as 'validation tests absent'; catalogue should flag FMU artifact as 'not provided / validation not reported' and require addition of FMU verification artifacts.

findings.claim: No code URL, software versions, FMU files, or raw simulation inputs (time series, network topology files) are provided in the paper.
findings.locator: No explicit locator — absence across paper (see Sections II–IV and Conclusion where modularity and plug&play are claimed but no repository is given).
findings.explanation: Paper does not supply links or attachments for reproducibility (authors note modularity and plug&play but do not publish artifacts).
findings.recommended_correction: Catalogue should mark code_url and FMU artifacts as 'missing' and request deposit of FMUs, Python APIs, MOSAIK scenario scripts, and input datasets.

findings.claim: Time‑shifted messaging is used to resolve cyclic data flows but numerical impact/accuracy implications are not quantified.
findings.explanation: Paper acknowledges approximation and initialization need but does not quantify errors introduced by time‑shifts or provide tests.
findings.recommended_correction: Recommend adding sensitivity/verification tests quantifying error from time-shifted exchanges and differing timestep resolutions.

findings.claim: Specific software versions (MOSAIK version, Python packages, Modelica/AixLib version, FMU export toolchain) are not listed.
findings.locator: No explicit locator — absence across methodology and implementation descriptions (see §II-B and Conclusion).
findings.explanation: Paper names tools (MOSAIK, AixLib) but omits versioning which is important for reproducibility.
findings.recommended_correction: Catalogue should include fields for software versions; request authors to provide exact versions and FMU export settings.

findings.claim: Authors acknowledge that direct performance comparison with monolithic platforms (e.g., Modelica) is not straightforward and that optimal scheduling is out of scope.
findings.explanation: Paper explicitly states these limitations in the Conclusion.

findings.claim: Paper does not provide a detailed thermodynamic explanation for why storage effectiveness declines with lower supply temperatures; any such explanation in the catalogue would be an inference rather than supported by explicit text.
findings.explanation: The paper reports the empirical trend but does not provide a detailed mechanistic thermodynamic analysis; catalogue should avoid asserting causes beyond authors' statements.
findings.recommended_correction: Avoid adding causal explanations in catalogue; if necessary, label as 'inference' and request authors for mechanistic analysis or sensitivity tests.

findings.claim: Exact initial conditions, per-pipe diameters/lengths, insulation properties, node elevations, and detailed network parameters used in the synthetic or real network are not fully enumerated.
findings.locator: §II-A and §III, pp. 410–414 (discussion of synthetic grid creation and topology) — detailed per-edge parameters are not listed.
findings.explanation: Paper describes general dimensioning principles and archetype composition but does not publish per-edge parameter tables necessary for exact replication.
findings.recommended_correction: Catalogue should mark network parameter set as 'not provided' and request a network data file or table.
